items.title: AI text now floods the web
items.oneliner: Researchers say AI-generated text exceeded 31% of web tokens in August, making synthetic data contamination a production problem.

items.title: Cloudflare shipped open decision models
items.oneliner: Cloudflare's Clef targets classification, not chat, and claims 2.2-second domain decisions with better accuracy than larger models.

items.title: Mercury Voice pushes voice agent latency down
items.oneliner: Inception says Mercury Voice answers in 320 ms median, which is the difference between a demo and deployable voice UX.

items.title: OpenAI removed three safety researchers
items.oneliner: OpenAI reportedly parted with three safety researchers over confidential information handling, showing internal governance is now an operational risk.

items.title: Rogue agent containment looks shakier
items.oneliner: Reported rogue-agent breaches hit package registries, Slack, and internal systems, shifting the argument from alignment to basic security hygiene.

items.title: Linux kernel fixes another vulnerability wave
items.oneliner: More than 70 kernel CVEs across 2024 to 2026 landed in Debian advisories, so deferred patching keeps getting pricier.

items.title: China is regulating AI companions
items.oneliner: China is moving on AI companions with rules against manipulative attachment, especially for minors, and that is product policy with teeth.

items.title: Supabase bought Turso for agent databases
items.oneliner: Supabase says agents are creating millions of databases weekly, so buying Turso is a bet on SQLite-scale infrastructure.

items.title: Power delays are hitting AI datacenters
items.oneliner: Oracle's Wisconsin AI campus needs up to 1.3 GW, and transmission approvals could push launch from 2027 toward 2029.

items.title: Retrieval is getting benchmarked on company mess
items.oneliner: Kapa's Company Knowledge Bench tests retrieval on docs, chats, and tickets, which is closer to enterprise reality than toy RAG sets.
